title: High-throughput drug screening of fine-needle aspiration-derived cancer organoids
protocol: Collect and wash organoids.
With a P1000 tip, pipette semi-solid cultures repetitively in a circular motion to break up the Matrigel.
Transfer cultures to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 340 × g for 5 min at 20°C–25°C and aspirate media.
Wash pelleted organoids with 10 mL cold PBS to remove any residual Matrigel or media, centrifuge as in step 1c, aspirate as much PBS as possible without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend organoids in 5 mL TrypLE and incubate at 37°C for 30 min, with vigorous pipetting every 10 min to break up cell clumps.
When close to single cell suspension or small clumps, centrifuge as in step 1c.
Aspirate TrypLE, then wash in warm modified DMEM media and centrifuge again as in step 1c.
Count cells.
Resuspend cells to a concentration of 9,500 cells/mL in complete DMEM + 2% Matrigel in a 50 mL conical tube.
Keep the cell suspension on ice prior to plating.
Plate the cell suspension immediately after preparation.
Equip BioTek EL406 peristaltic pump with a 10 μL wide-bore tip cassette and set to low speed.
Swirl the tube of cells prior to priming the tubing and before each plate to ensure equal suspension dispensing.
Dispense 30 μl cell suspension per well into the cell-repellent microplates.
Dispense 10 μL of treatment at 4× the desired concentration into wells of each plate, including replicates and appropriate vehicle controls.
Incubate plates at 37°C, 5% CO2 for the desired treatment time (24–96 h).
Add propidium iodide to wells to a final concentration of 5 μg/mL, 24 hours prior to drug treatment end.
Incubate with propidium iodide at 37°C for 24 h.
Add Hoechst to the wells at a final concentration of 10 μg/mL.
Incubate with Hoechst at 37°C for 2 h.
Add Calcein AM to the wells at a final concentration of 5 μM.
Incubate with Calcein AM for 1 hour.
Image the samples with a fluorescence microscope.
Check the wells under a microscope following this step to ensure that all organoids have been broken up.
Repeat vigorous pipetting as necessary until none remain.
Make sure not to introduce bubbles when mixing.
Place plates on a plate shaker for 25 min at up to 800 RPMs.
Centrifuge the plates to eliminate any bubbles and draw liquid to the bottom of the well.
Quantify luminescence with a plate reader.
Determine drug effect by subtracting control luminescence from treatment luminescence.
Plot the result against drug concentration for each treatment using Excel or GraphPad Prism.
